title: A prior-summer heat and rain interaction raised next-summer rain error across 344 US divisions in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether prior-summer temperature and its rain interaction improve next-summer rain estimates across 344 US climate divisions. Each fit used earlier target years only in NOAA nClimDiv data. For 45 test years in 1981-2025, adding the two terms raised variance-scaled squared error by 4.80% beyond prior rain and a linear time trend. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for the increase was 1.55% to 8.39%. Temperature alone gave an uncertain 0.25% reduction. The interaction beyond temperature raised error by 5.06%. One- and five-year blocks, squared-rain control and recent training fits retained the negative full-model score. No single scoring year caused its sign. This is a test of a local continuous interaction at a long lead. It does not refute land feedbacks or measure water-store recovery. One revised product, simple models and conditional intervals limit inference. The package gives code, national scores, source hashes, a figure, an audit and retrieval instructions. External source records and full forecast tables stay outside the bundle.
